sources.name: 14 Countries Where Drinking Alcohol Is Illegal

_: Illegal in Gujarat, Nagaland, Bihar and Mizoram.
Illegal for Muslims and in public.
A license is required; alcohol is illegal during Ramadan.
Illegal in public places and during Ramadan.
Home production legal for Zoroastrians, Jews and Christians.
Illegal in public, legal in hotels, restaurants, bars and homes.
Banned by parliament, but rarely enforced.
Alcohol must be purchased and consumed in licensed hotels, bars, and tourist area, or in major supermarkets.
Public drinking illegal in Kelantan and Terengganu.
Complete ban enforced from 1952 to 2024, now accessible to foreign non-Muslim diplomats as well as select non-Muslim residents making over 50,000 riyals a month or holding premium residency.
Sales partially restricted for Muslims since 2024; exceptions apply for non-Muslim population such as Christians
Alcohol sales are banned on Fridays and during Ramadan.
Illegal in Sharjah and in public.
Selling in stores between 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. is illegal; serving at bars, restaurants and clubs always legal.
Illegal on trains, airplanes, and ferries and in sports facilities. Sales are banned on weekends and holidays, except at bars and restaurants.
Illegal in Gaza, legal in West Bank
Legal for non-Muslim foreigners at restaurants, hotels and bars; at home with a licence. Illegal in public
Illegal in public, except at bars and restaurants. Alcohol is only sold in stores within a certain time period on weekdays
Selling in stores between 10:30 p.m. to 10:30 a.m. (12:30 p.m. on Sundays) is illegal; pubs are confined to set hours for sale of alcohol.
Legal for tourists at hotels and bars as well as expatriates with permits.
Legal for foreigners at licensed establishments; transport of alcohol is illegal.
Non-Muslims over 17 years old are allowed a limited amount of alcohol, but they must consume it in private.
